Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with increasing yellow discoloration of your eyes and skin; have you noticed this color changing or spreading since birth?

To help me assess this further, could you tell me if your baby was breastfed exclusively, and were there any complications during the birth or jaundice present at delivery?

REQUEST TEST: Total_Bilirubin_Levels
REQUEST TEST: Direct_Bilirubin_Levels

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Jaundice due to Breastfeeding Insufficiency (Physiological Jaundice). The total bilirubin of 16.1 mg/dL with a normal direct bilirubin (0.7 mg/dL) indicates isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, which is characteristic of common neonatal jaundice. No immediate exchange transfusion is required at this level unless symptoms of acute bilirubin encephalopathy are present, but close monitoring and increased feeding are indicated.

Please confirm: Is the baby feeding well and wetting at least 6-8 diapers per day?
